context:
Goal: a lane's lint result means the same as CI's.
Problem (rule): merging main into #1938 clashes in bin/ci-job and merge/merge.py. Main has `pin_tree` (a git archive) and a `--pinned` flag set by merge's ready check; the PR has a worktree-based pinned tree with signal cleanup and a dead-run sweep. One of them has to go.
Based on (ruling): your 11:53 CST pick of 714 b (lane lint follows the pinned trees, child repos too).
Departs from: main — main runs ste-lint local with a drift note; a runs it pinned and drops `--pinned`.

options.gain: One pinned path, no worktree sweep to maintain.
options.how: ste-lint under --lint runs the pinned copy; the PR's worktree machinery is not used.
options.label: Keep `pin_tree`, port the per-step pins onto it, drop `--pinned` (coordinator's pick)
options.lose: The PR's own worktree design is dropped.

options.label: Keep the PR's worktree machinery; retire `pin_tree` and `--pinned`
options.lose: More code to keep clean (signal cleanup, dead-run sweep).

reply: The retrospective agrees with a (12:15 CST Nov 13), with one addition: `pin_tree` must first resolve a moving ref (714 b's stable branch, the same one CI uses) to its commit, then archive that commit. Today only a sha pin works in `pinned_file`. The addition goes on step lane-lint-runs-local-tools and to the lane. This stays open for your veto.

shown.label: Keep `pin_tree`, port the per-step pins onto it, drop `--pinned` (coordinator's pick)
Keep the PR's worktree machinery; retire `pin_tree` and `--pinned`

title: For lane lint following pinned trees (#1938), keep main's `pin_tree` archive and drop `--pinned`?
why: The coordinator took this pick on your 714 b; it stands unless you choose b (a third option, keeping both, breaks one home per capability).
